title: Tan v. South Texas Presbytery
disposition_detail: The SJC declared TE Tan's complaint administratively out of order as not timely filed under BCO 43-3 and SJC Manual 10.1(a), 19.10(b); no merits ruling was reached. Vote: 22 concur, 1 recused, 1 absent.
first_summary: The SJC dismissed TE Tan's complaint against South Texas Presbytery as untimely. The complaint, dated and faxed August 28, 1999, was not mailed until September 4 and was received September 7, exceeding BCO 43-3's 30-day filing period. SJC Manual 19.10 allows filing by certified, registered, or express mail, not fax. The merits were not reached. Twenty-two members concurred, one recused, and one was absent.
summary: Tan's complaint challenged South Texas Presbytery's action at its July 30–31, 1999 meeting. The SJC declared the complaint administratively out of order because it was untimely under BCO 43-3: although dated and faxed August 28, it was not mailed until September 4 and was received September 7—beyond 30 days. SJC Manual 19.10 requires receipt in the Stated Clerk's office and disallows fax filing. The merits were not reached. Twenty-two members concurred; one was recused and one absent.
